content.text: Modal systems differ in which principles they accept. Each one below adds an axiom to the one before it.

symbols.name: □(P → Q) → (□P → □Q)
symbols.meaning: Necessity carries over an if then.

symbols.name: □P → □□P
symbols.meaning: What is necessary is necessarily necessary.

symbols.name: ◇P → □◇P
symbols.meaning: What is possible is necessarily possible.

content.text: Logical necessity is often modeled with S5.

examples.title: T in words
lines: If P is necessary, then P is true.
examples.note: A logic of what ought to be drops this axiom, since what ought to happen often does not.

examples.title: S5 in words
lines: If P is possible, then it is necessarily possible.
examples.note: In S5, what is possible does not depend on which world you start from.

question.prompt: What does the T axiom □P → P say?
options: Necessity and possibility are the same
question.explanation: □P → P says that if P is necessary, then P is true.
